label: License map: OpenBot, OpenGhost and hermes-muse are MIT; buzz, turnstone, rakazo and OpenMausBot are Apache-2.0; openhuman is GPL-3.0-only.
OpenBot shared/tool-name.ts (MIT) exports approvalWords and approvalPhrase, the pure action-kind classifier for delete, send, share, post and pay.
OpenBot shared/standing-rule.ts (MIT) exports offersStandingRule, which decides when a one-off allowance may become a standing rule.
OpenBot shared/activity-rows.ts and app/src/lib/bot-lifecycle/activity-groups.ts (MIT) are the activity vocabulary and seven-group ordering as pure functions.
OpenBot app/src/lib/routines/plan.ts (MIT) is the answers-to-plan mapping for routine, goal and check-in, adaptable to a bots routine new command.
Turnstone turnstone/core/memory.py and memory_index.py (Apache-2.0) implement typed, scoped structured memory and are reusable with license, NOTICE and a statement of changes.
OpenMausBot src/state/team-chats.ts (Apache-2.0) is small per-team chat ownership state outside the enterprise carve-out.
openhuman-tui is GPL-3.0-only at workspace and crate level, so its code cannot be copied into an MIT or Apache project without relicensing the combined work.

Ranked lifts: activity groups and rows, then tool-name classifier, then routines plan (all MIT), then turnstone memory (Apache-2.0), then team-chats state (Apache-2.0); everything else is reference-only.

Attribution mechanics: MIT needs the copyright and permission notice; Apache-2.0 needs the license, any NOTICE and a statement of changes; one THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES entry per lifted file with source path and commit satisfies both.

reason: GPL-3.0-only would force the combined work under GPL.
